Thanks again for the demo earlier — helpful conversation. A quick recap of the items our security and infra teams asked to clarify so we can move this along: 

1) Identity/SSO
- We need SAML 2.0 and OIDC support for single sign-on, plus SCIM for automatic user provisioning into your console. Is SCIM required for Dedicated/Private only, or supported with hosted accounts?

2) Key management / HSM
- We must use HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) for certain workloads. We also need BYOK with key import and a documented key rotation policy. Can Redwood integrate with our AWS CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM, or does that mandate Private deployment?

3) Audit logs & retention
- Compliance requires immutable audit logs retained for 7 years and the ability to forward logs to our Splunk instance (TLS syslog or HTTPS ingest). Does Redwood support long-term retention and log-forwarding from both Dedicated and Private?

4) Network / egress constraints
- We operate in a locked-down VPC. We'll need details on required ports, whether VPC peering or Transit Gateway is supported, and if egress billing differs between Dedicated and Private.

Next steps we need from Redwood: a short architecture note showing where keys live for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, a sample network diagram for Private VPC, and a clear statement on which deployment modes meet the HSM requirement. Also please share your SOC2 report and any relevant attachments.

Can we schedule a 60-minute technical call next week with your SE and our infra/security folks? Wednesday/Thursday AM PST works for us.

Thanks,
Jordan
VP Product, Fintegral

Jordan — appreciate the clear list. Confirming we captured everything and outlining immediate next steps from our side. 

Short answers up front:
- SSO: Hosted supports SAML and OIDC for API/console access; SCIM provisioning is available for Hosted & Dedicated.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) are supported for envelope encryption on Hosted, but if you need an HSM-backed key where private material never leaves your HSM (CloudHSM / Dedicated HSM) we typically recommend Private deployment. There are hybrid options (Dedicated with private KMS peering) — Marcus can elaborate.
- Logs: Redwood supports real-time log forwarding to Splunk or S3; long-term immutable retention (7+ yrs) is supported on Private and on Dedicated with our compliance add-on. Hosted has configurable retention but for immutable, air-gapped archives we route to the customer's storage.
- Network: We'll prepare a sample network diagram showing VPC peering, Transit Gateway options, and firewall ports. Egress billing differs on Dedicated (reserved capacity flat) vs Hosted (standard cloud egress).

Action items (we'll own):
- Marcus: prepare an architecture note + network diagram showing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private key flows and where HSMs sit. Attach: redwood-deploy-mode-comparison-20260914.xlsx and network-diagram-sample.png.
- Laura: pull SOC2 report and redact as needed, add to thread.
- Myself: propose 2 slots for a technical deep-dive (Weds/Thurs AM PST) and draft a short mutual action plan/estimate for Dedicated vs Private pricing.

I'll follow up with the calendar invite once Marcus confirms the SE availability.

Jordan / team — adding technical color to help your infra/security assess options. Below is a pragmatic breakdown and what typically drives customers to Dedicated vs Private.

1) Identity/SCIM
- Hosted: SAML/OIDC supported; SCIM provisioning available — we can connect to your IdP (Okta/AzureAD) for user sync. No extra infra required.
- Dedicated/Private: Same support; for Private we can also integrate with on-prem AD via LDAP over a customer VPN if needed.

2) Keys and HSMs
- Hosted: We support customer-managed keys using AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault (envelope encryption). Keys are HSM-protected at the cloud provider level, but key material lifecycle is controlled via cloud KMS policies. For customers requiring the private HSM boundary (CloudHSM where key material never leaves your HSM), Private deployment is the recommended path.
- Dedicated: We offer a Dedicated variant where we can set up a dedicated key-hosting arrangement (bring-your-own-key backed by a customer-managed cloud HSM) and private peering to the KMS. This often satisfies customers that need stronger separation but not full on-prem. There are additional networking and compliance steps — I'll call these out in the architecture note.

3) Audit logs & retention
- Log forwarding: Splunk (syslog TLS), S3/GCS archival, or HTTPS ingest are supported from all deployment modes.
- Immutable retention: For Hosted we can forward and store logs in your account (S3) with lifecycle rules you control. For Dedicated and Private we can host retention policies as part of the offering and provide write-once buckets / WORM policies if you need a managed solution.

4) Networking and throughput
- Private: best for strict VPC control, direct HSM access, and long-term retention inside your network.
- Dedicated: hits a sweet spot when you want predictable latency and reserved GPU pools but still keep keys in your managed KMS.
- Hosted: fastest time-to-value; good for evaluation and many production use-cases without extreme HSM requirements.

I'll attach a short architecture note (see redwood-deploy-mode-comparison-20260914.xlsx) and a sample network diagram. I recommend the following next steps:
- Technical deep-dive (60m) with your infra/security + our SE (I'll lead the session and bring our infra PM)
- If HSM is required: sign an NDA addendum and we'll scope Private vs Dedicated HSM peering (rough timeline: 6-10 weeks for Private onboarding, 3-6 weeks for Dedicated peering depending on cloud approvals)
- I'll include an initial pricing delta for Reserved Dedicated capacity vs Private in the MAP.

Happy to walk through the architecture on the call. Proposed slots: Wed 09/16 09:30 or Wed 09/16 11:00 PST. Let me know which works.

—Marcus
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
